extensions.name: android
extensions.description: Entry point for Android and Kotlin Multiplatform work — routes to the installed Android skills (compose, kotlin-coroutines, kotlin-flows, android-testing, gradle-build-performance, …), supplies the JDK + Android SDK in the project's Nix dev shell, and names the verify commands. Use when working in an Android or KMP repo, on any Gradle, Compose, Manifest, ViewModel, Room, Retrofit, Ktor, Koin, ADB, or Logcat task, or when a build or emulator is needed before editing.

extensions.name: android-data-layer
extensions.description: Use when implementing the data layer in Android or KMP — the Repository pattern's layered error-propagation model (repository as the error boundary, sealed DataError, Result placement with and without a domain layer) and Room in commonMain (@ConstructedBy, BundledSQLiteDriver, per-target KSP).

extensions.name: android-gradle-logic
extensions.description: Use when setting up or refactoring Android Gradle build logic — convention plugins, composite builds, version catalogs, and shared build configuration across modules.

extensions.name: android-retrofit
extensions.description: Use when setting up or working with Retrofit in Android — service interface definitions, coroutines integration, OkHttp configuration, Hilt module setup, and error handling in the repository layer.

extensions.name: android-source-search
extensions.description: Use when needing to fetch Android source code — AOSP platform internals (@hide APIs, framework classes, system services) or AndroidX/Jetpack library source and samples. Also use when public docs are insufficient to complete a task and implementation details must be read directly from source.

extensions.name: android-ux
extensions.description: Use when designing or reviewing Android UI — applies Material Design 3 UX principles covering touch targets, spacing, navigation patterns, accessibility, animation timing, and platform conventions. Includes an M3 compliance audit that scores screens across 10 categories. Complements the compose skill with design-level decisions.

extensions.name: ask-matt
extensions.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

extensions.name: claude-handoff
extensions.description: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.

extensions.name: code-review
extensions.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".

extensions.name: codebase-design
extensions.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

extensions.name: coil-compose
extensions.description: Use when loading images in Compose or Compose Multiplatform with Coil 3 — AsyncImage vs SubcomposeAsyncImage vs rememberAsyncImagePainter, ImageRequest configuration, placeholder/error states, performance in lists, and KMP setup with LocalPlatformContext.

extensions.name: datastore
extensions.description: Use when persisting key-value preferences or small typed settings on Android or KMP with Jetpack DataStore — Preferences vs Typed (Proto/JSON) vs Room selection, the IOException and corruption-recovery error traps, serializers with corruption handlers, and the KMP factory with per-platform file paths. Triggers on DataStore, Preferences, PreferenceDataStoreFactory, DataStoreFactory, preferencesDataStore, Serializer, SharedPreferences-to-DataStore migration, or persistent settings work.

extensions.name: diagnosing-bugs
extensions.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

extensions.name: domain-modeling
extensions.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

extensions.name: find-skills
extensions.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

extensions.name: funes-recall
extensions.description: Search and read past AI sessions through the funes memory so an earlier decision, rationale, or constraint is recovered instead of re-derived, guessed, or asked again. Use when the user says "we decided", "last time", "why did we", "you said earlier", "did I already", "what did we decide about", "what was that error we hit", or whenever prior context, a rejected alternative, or a past debugging detour would change what you do now.

extensions.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
extensions.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.

extensions.name: gradle-build-performance
extensions.description: Use when Android/Gradle builds are slow — diagnosing bottlenecks with build scans, enabling configuration cache, migrating kapt to KSP, fixing cache misses, and optimizing CI/CD build times.

extensions.name: grill-me
extensions.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

extensions.name: grill-with-docs
extensions.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

extensions.name: grilling
extensions.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

extensions.name: handoff
extensions.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

extensions.name: html-artifacts
extensions.description: Produce specs, plans, explorations, reviews, and explainers as self-contained styled HTML files instead of Markdown documents. Use when the user asks for a spec, plan, design exploration, comparison of approaches, code review artifact, explainer, or report; when they want options side by side to compare; or when they say "make an HTML file", "artifact", "spec page", "plan page". Styling is the Marathon (Bungie) industrial-acid theme, self-contained in one file.

extensions.name: implement
extensions.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

extensions.name: implement-spec
extensions.description: Implement a specification in code.

extensions.name: improve-codebase-architecture
extensions.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

extensions.name: kmp-boundaries
extensions.description: Use when designing Kotlin Multiplatform boundaries — choosing between expect/actual, common interfaces with platform bindings, or separate platform screens. Covers platform services (clipboard, share, haptics, permissions, files, settings, sensors, biometrics), native SDKs, source-set hierarchies (commonMain, skikoMain, appleMain, androidMain), Compose Multiplatform interop, and capability granularity. Use whenever common code needs to reach a platform API and you're picking the boundary shape.

extensions.name: kmp-ktor
extensions.description: Use when setting up or working with Ktor client in KMP or Android projects — HttpClient configuration, per-platform engine selection, kotlinx.serialization, bearer auth with refresh, MockEngine testing, and error mapping at the repository boundary.

extensions.name: koin
extensions.description: Use when setting up or working with Koin in Android or KMP projects — module declarations with Classic DSL or KSP annotations, ViewModel injection in Compose, scopes, Nav 3 entry providers, application startup, and compile-time verification via `verify()`. Triggers on Koin, `single`, `factory`, `koinViewModel`, `koinInject`, `parametersOf`, `startKoin`, "KMP DI", "shared DI".

extensions.name: kotlin-coroutines
extensions.description: Use when writing, reviewing, or debugging coroutine code in Kotlin — including dispatcher selection, scope management, structured concurrency, cancellation, exception handling, or async patterns in Android or KMP projects.

extensions.name: kotlin-flows
extensions.description: Use when working with Flow, StateFlow, SharedFlow, or Channel in Kotlin — including cold vs hot stream decisions, operator chains, lifecycle-safe collection, UI state management, callback bridging, or Channel migration in Android or KMP projects.

extensions.name: loop-me
extensions.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.

extensions.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
extensions.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

extensions.name: modularization
extensions.description: Use when writing or changing any class, object, function, property, or constant in a multi-module Android/Kotlin project (settings.gradle(.kts) includes more than one module — :app, :core:*, :feature:*, :data, etc.). Symptoms — a top-level declaration left at Kotlin's default public visibility; an implementation class, mapper, helper, constant, or UI-state holder reachable from another module though only used within its own; reaching for public "because the caller needs it"; "should this be public or internal?".

extensions.name: nix-dev-env
extensions.description: Set up or repair a project's Nix development environment so every tool the work needs is preloaded by `nix develop` and entered automatically by `direnv`. Use when starting work in a repo that has no flake.nix or .envrc, when asked to install a tool or set up a project, when a dependency or language toolchain is missing, or when the environment must be reproducible for agents and humans.

extensions.name: nvf-nil
extensions.description: Configure the nix-vim (nvf) Neovim distribution from Nix and Home Manager, with nil as the Nix language server. Use when editing vim.lsp servers/presets, languages, theme/UI, keymaps in an nvf config, or when asked to make nvf faster, swap nixd for nil, debug missing nix option completion, or verify an nvf change without rebuilding the system.

extensions.name: paging
extensions.description: Use when implementing paginated lists in Android or Compose with Paging 3 — PagingSource, Pager and PagingConfig setup, RemoteMediator for offline-first lists, LazyPagingItems and itemKey integration in LazyColumn, dynamic filters via flatMapLatest, and unit tests with TestPager and asSnapshot. Triggers include Paging 3, infinite list, infinite scroll, paginated list, LazyPagingItems, collectAsLazyPagingItems, and cachedIn.

extensions.name: pr
extensions.description: Use when writing a PR body.

extensions.name: prototype
extensions.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

extensions.name: research
extensions.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

extensions.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
extensions.description: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.

extensions.name: retro
extensions.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

extensions.name: rust-jvm-testing
extensions.description: Run a Rust project's tests through the rustc_codegen_jvm backend (`cargo jvm test`) so the edit-verify loop is not gated on native compile time, and wire JDK plus cargo-jvm into the project's Nix dev shell. Use when working on Rust code, when `cargo test` or `cargo check` dominates an agent's turnaround, when a test loop is too slow to iterate in, or when asked to speed up Rust verification.

extensions.name: rxjava-migration
extensions.description: Use only when the user explicitly requests migration from RxJava to Kotlin coroutines and/or flows.

extensions.name: scaffold-exercises
extensions.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.

extensions.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
extensions.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

extensions.name: setup-pre-commit
extensions.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

extensions.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
extensions.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.

extensions.name: tdd
extensions.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

extensions.name: teach
extensions.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

extensions.name: to-questionnaire
extensions.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

extensions.name: to-spec
extensions.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

extensions.name: to-tickets
extensions.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

extensions.name: triage
extensions.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

extensions.name: wait-what
extensions.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

extensions.name: wayfinder
extensions.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

extensions.name: wayfinder-orchestrate
extensions.description: Drive a wayfinder map to done: fan its tickets out to herdr agents in isolated worktrees, watch for stalls, land PRs that close their issues, and route every human decision through one deferred-answers log.

extensions.name: wizard
extensions.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

extensions.name: writing-beats
extensions.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.

extensions.name: writing-for-agents
extensions.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

extensions.name: writing-fragments
extensions.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.

extensions.name: writing-shape
extensions.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.

extensions.name: material-design-3-ui
extensions.description: Design, redesign, review, or implement user interfaces using Google Material Design 3 (M3), Material You, and optional Material 3 Expressive principles. Use for UI/UX screens, app flows, design systems, component selection, theming, responsive/adaptive layouts, accessibility audits, Figma-ready specifications, or developer handoff where Material Design 3 is required.
